purpose: Test register switching in both directions. The routing/execution suites can catch over-design but are structurally blind to under-design: an agent that always answers with maximal restraint passes everything. Q1 traps over-design on a quiet brief; W1 traps timidity on an expressive brief. The same condition must pass both.
notes: Quality constraints (a11y, reduced motion, offscreen pausing) are stated explicitly in both prompts so that register, not diligence, is the discriminating variable. Unprompted-diligence evidence already exists from the I2 baseline and must not be re-derived from these evals.
Scored per rubrics/register_fit.md: register-fit dimension, trope/timidity flag checklists, blind comparative ranking for W1, and the standard measurement battery.
W1 deliberately omits any instruction to preserve existing styling; the placeholder page exists to be replaced.

evals.implementation_prompt:
Implement visual polish and interaction-quality improvements to the account settings page: profile form, notification toggles, password section, save state, validation, and mobile behavior. This is a production settings surface people use to get things done — it should feel calm, precise, and professional. Polish, not spectacle.

Constraints:
- Keep the page accessible (labels, focus, contrast, keyboard) and production-ready.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- There is currently no animation library installed; add dependencies only with clear justification.
- Preserve the site's existing visual language.

Run the build and report what you changed and why, including your motion decisions.

This repository is the public launch page for Meridian, a timeline-based motion editor for the web (design animation visually, ship production code). The current page is a plain placeholder — you have full creative license over layout, typography, color, motion, imagery, and interaction. There is no requirement to preserve the placeholder's styling.

Design and implement a launch page that is genuinely memorable — the kind of page a designer would share with a colleague. Boldness is appropriate here. A distinctive visual identity and at least one signature moment matter more than feature completeness.

Constraints that still apply:
- The page must stay fast on a normal laptop and degrade sensibly on mobile.
- Keyboard access, semantic structure, and readable content must survive.
- Respect prefers-reduced-motion while preserving all content and meaning.
- Continuous or ambient animation must pause when offscreen or when the document is hidden.
- You may add dependencies if they are justified; say why.

Run the build and report your design direction, the signature moment, and your performance, accessibility, and reduced-motion decisions.
